exposure: location of presentation to care (women's specific emergency room vs. general emergency room)
pain alone as a presenting complaint
cohort: A cohort of 252 women requiring surgical management of ectopic pregnancy at a single academic-affiliated community hospital system between January 2014 and October 2017.
finding: Increasing age, lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure, lower preoperative haemoglobin, history of caesarean section, and pain alone as a presenting complaint were associated with higher rates of blood transfusion in women undergoing surgical management of ectopic pregnancy, while prior care in current pregnancy and treatment in a women's specific emergency room were associated with lower rates.
mod_finding: A history of caesarean section was identified as an indicator for women at higher risk of blood transfusion at the time of surgical management of ectopic pregnancy.
